```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from IPython.display import Markdown
from datasets import load_dataset
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
```

## Overview

Compare a TF-IDF classifier with an LLM on the same sentiment classification task using 20 sample reviews.

## Task 1: Select 20 Test Reviews

Choose 20 reviews (10 positive, 10 negative) from your test set. These should include some easy cases and some tricky ones (sarcasm, negation, mixed sentiment).

## Task 2: Classify with Your TF-IDF Model

```{python, warning=FALSE}
# Use your pipeline from P12.1
# tfidf_preds = pipe.predict(sample_reviews)
dataset = load_dataset("stanfordnlp/imdb", split="train").shuffle(seed=42).select(range(5000))
texts = dataset["text"]
labels = dataset["label"]

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(texts, labels, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

pipe = Pipeline([
    ("tfidf", TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2), stop_words="english")),
    ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
])
pipe.fit(X_train, y_train)
```

```{python}
test = pd.DataFrame({"text": X_test, "label": y_test})
test["label"] = test["label"].map({1: "pos", 0: "neg"})
test["text_clean"] = test["text"].str.replace("<br />", " ", regex=False)  # for display/LLM
test["n_words"] = test["text_clean"].str.split().str.len()
print(test.head(20))
```

## Task 3: Classify with an LLM

Use Claude, ChatGPT, or another LLM (via web interface or API) to classify the same 20 reviews. Document the prompt you used.

**Your prompt:** *You are a sentiment classifier for movie reviews. For each numbered review below, answer with exactly one word: positive or negative. Return one line per review in the format "<number>: <label>" and nothing else.*
